event.detail:
Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333

## TLDR
Deleting periodic old-terminal warning tests agrees with the release's intentional removal of old terminals.

## Details
Considered whether deleting the three old-terminal notification lifecycle tests leaves users unaware of running old agents or resolves warnings too early. SPEC.md:2799-2809 (Status; exact passage located in the full section read) explicitly says: "That release is this one, so no warning is recorded any more, and every supervisor start marks any unresolved one resolved." It also specifies a new notice for each still-live old agent ended at startup. This replaces, rather than preserves, the deleted tests' contracts of one periodic warning while old agent/tab panes remain live. core.rs:6144-6151 starts the old-server termination step for the owning supervisor; :7077-7091 invokes old_terminals::record_ended after committed conversion, even with no converted rows; core/old_terminals.rs:517-546 documents and implements recording the new notice and resolving the old warning kind. No periodic old-terminal warning is now expected.
Suggested bucket: other (not reported). Confidence: confirmed by source and specification, no execution. proposed_drop: true; explicit specification replacement quoted above, corroborated by startup callers. Could-be-highest: no established security or loss-of-work consequence from deleting these notification tests; the intentional old-process termination is specified behavior outside this test-deletion concern. possible_cover: none; coverage sources not consulted. Caveat: this checks the assigned notification-test removal and replacement's caller contract, not an independent audit of all old-terminal termination mechanics.

event.summary: Single-pass persistence test does not establish host catch-up
event.detail:
Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333

## TLDR
The converted test takes one status sample without establishing that its newly adopted terminal is eligible for sampling. A source-permitted multi-event adoption can leave that pass skipping the fixture and failing its persistence assertions. Whether this exact short-line fixture produces the required event split is unverified after investigation; no failure was observed. This concerns test reliability, not user data or a verified product failure.

## Details
Contract: the supplied test checklist requires the fixture premise before the action and the named readiness boundary. ticker.rs:1331-1338 selects a terminal only when caught_up and owned-live. The changed test starts the host at :5213, installs a durable row, seeds four recognized Waiting observations at :5227-5240, and runs exactly one sample_pass at :5251 before requiring Running, the in-memory/durable START key and no pending retry at :5253-5279. Neither spawn_host (:1858-1891), install_durable_running_entry (:1960-2010), nor the caller waits for caught_up. Database awaits supply no ordering contract with the terminal runtime.

Useful additional checks and results in this synthesis: (1) hosts/client.rs:789-813 sends only Read and Info in the adoption exchange; :1103-1142 queues stream records/acknowledgements as HostEvents but handles InfoReply separately. hosts/terminal.rs:2681-2708 pins the child using Info only. (2) terminal-host/src/journal.rs:139-155 initializes this no-snapshot journal with no resizes, no gap and no exit, and :344-394 starts a default-position Read directly in its tail. The fixture sends no input/resize, and sleeps after printf. host.rs:548-568 and :582-623 acknowledge only resolved input. Therefore an initial InfoReply, Welcome, zero-input acknowledgement, snapshot, resize or gap is not a concrete extra-event route for this healthy fixture. (3) More than one output event is source-permitted even though the line fits in one storage block. host.rs:344-369 reads currently available PTY data, writes already-queued frames, then handles client messages; :407-411 refills after them. :503-537 stops PTY draining on EAGAIN. :628-650 materializes Output frames immediately and advances the journal cursor. journal.rs:207-229 coalesces new bytes in storage, but :447-469 copies bytes from the cursor's current offset; later bytes cannot merge into a previously queued frame or rewind that cursor.

Conditional concrete enqueue sequence, rather than a generic scheduling assertion: Read is handled in a loop before the first Info and refill queues O1 for the bytes then available. A later loop drains additional bytes, writes O1, handles Info1 (queues Reply1), then refills O2. The client receives Reply1 and O2, sends Info2, and its second Info round trip can decode both O1 and O2 before returning. hosts/client.rs:1016-1030 decodes buffered frames before checking request completion, and :1078-1099 decodes every whole frame. Adoption's fence is then at least two (hosts/terminal.rs:1821). It processes only one queued event at :1916-1926, decrements the fence once (:3343-3344), and spawns the background runtime (:1928). Its status remains caught_up=false until the remaining fenced event is processed (:4008-4027). If sample selection precedes that processing, it skips the entry, preserves seeded Waiting and never allocates START. There is no source-level readiness dependency that prevents this final ordering. An explicit bounded wait for the adopted handle's caught_up/owned-live state before this one-pass stimulus would address that eligibility contract.

Exact remaining premise and confidence limit: the unmodified platform sh/printf and PTY must expose this particular short line in available chunks separated across the host's loop/refill boundaries; repository source does not contain that shell's output implementation or specify atomic visibility of its output on the PTY. A second raw read within the same drain would coalesce before refill and would not suffice. No claim is made that this split occurred, is common, or is forced by the source. The queue/control ordering permits it; the current source does not establish or refute its occurrence for the external fixture. This is unverified after investigation, retained as a finding under the caller's requested disposition, not a confirmed flake. Evidence that settles the remaining premise could be platform shell/PTY source guarantees covering this write and read visibility, or existing instrumentation showing the exact output/refill/fence/caught_up ordering at the sample boundary. A failure trace is not required to identify the missing readiness contract; none was demanded, generated or observed. No reproduction or runtime experiment was requested or performed.

Separate original consequence and proposed-drop basis preserved: the initial producer-frame concern was a false pass on blank startup text instead of literal 'work resumed'. That argument is source-refuted for this test's actual transition/persistence subject. A blank screen differing from the seeded Claude dialog legitimately yields generic Working through ticker.rs:586-639 and agent_kind/screen_reader.rs:365-375, :575-592; that still exercises the asserted transition, allocation and durable write. Parent ticker.rs:7147-7227 already used the same manually seeded dialog, printf command and assertions, without a frame oracle (parent spawn_pane :2379-2390). Literal producer text is not a necessary assertion. This source-based proposed drop does not refute the separate new host catch-up eligibility question. Earlier 'normally first record' wording is superseded; typical behavior and absence of observed failure are not proof.

Suggested bucket: other (maintainer test reliability if the remaining premise holds). Confidence: unverified after investigation for the concrete failure; source-confirmed missing explicit readiness dependency and enqueue sequence conditional on separated output availability. proposed_drop: false for the catch-up issue; true only for the separately preserved producer-text argument, on the exact source basis above, not specification acceptance. Could-be-highest: no; no security or user-work-loss route. possible_cover: none; coverage sources not consulted. Caller has accepted no drop. All conclusions are source-derived, not execution observations.

The deleted mismatched-pane-name test guarded tmux's recyclable pane IDs. Current sampling reads the entry's terminal runtime directly, so that deleted lookup cannot accidentally sample another session.
